Open Air.
Skin, cloth & the public body.

Ceremony can envelop the body.
Everyday life can leave it open.

01 · Lin Wei’s correction

Coverage is a choice
we have to design.

“Only the formal ceremonial wear should feel clothed. The rest, we can explore being bare chested for guys etc. let’s not be too prudish about it.”

This volume revises the heavily layered default of the previous pass. Bare chests, open vests, single-shoulder cloth, waist wraps, short aprons and exposed limbs become ordinary possibilities in this equatorial world.

What changes

The school’s identity moves toward its waist, fold, fastening, carried object, footwear and headwear. The shirt becomes one surface among many for displaying belonging.

The male adult figure is the focus of this first open-body study. The range of physiques and other wearers should broaden as the garment families develop.

What stays deliberate

Ceremonial dress keeps its fuller silhouette. Everyday openness is an option. Field clothing responds to the actual work; sport clothing responds to the actual movement.

The Seven still have different relationships to value, duty, repair, sound and shared use. Taking off a shirt reveals those differences.

Design status: the new direction follows Lin Wei’s brief. Specific route C cuts, relocated identifiers and headwear below are new directions. Parts I and II record earlier development; this exploration opens their full-coverage daily assumptions.

03 · A controlled occasion change

One island.
Four ways to dress.

Compare the same seven adult construction figures across occasions. The fuller ceremonial figures are carried forward from Part II; the other three are newly drawn.

Field figures are light-duty construction concepts. A sun cover, weather layer, flotation or other protection is added when the actual task calls for it.

04 · Seven revised wardrobe families

What carries belonging
when the chest is bare?

01 · Parallax · route C

Toa Keng Institution

Articulated geometry

Where the identifier moves

The four-button jacket and disputed tie remain available for ceremony. The narrow silt marker migrates to the waist for casual wear.

Feet and ground

Low walking shoes for daily use; flexible training soles for footwork; task-specific field grip.

02 · Amanah · route C

Al-Merikani College

Controlled disclosure

Where the identifier moves

The inward-facing heirloom rule moves from jacket lining to waist facing or an inner belt. The visible patterned coat becomes a choice for occasions.

Feet and ground

Low deck shoes for daily use; sport and wet-work soles selected separately.

03 · Communion · route C

Sri Temenggong Institution

The practised fold

Where the identifier moves

The kain remains. Full-length trousers become one option among several. Shoe removal at the Balai Lama remains place-specific.

Feet and ground

Removable sandals for daily movement; barefoot for the depicted clean training floor; protective field footwear as the task requires.

04 · Recomposition · route C

Lan Fang College · 兰芳书院

Visible revision

Where the identifier moves

The date formerly placed at the cuff can move to hem, waistband or an exposed joining tab when sleeves are absent. Each cohort keeps its own location rule.

Feet and ground

Slim walking shoes for daily use; grip soles for movement practice; work-specific protection.

05 · Reciprocity · route C

House of Nine Rain

The material account

Where the identifier moves

The earlier full heavy-cotton work tunic becomes a ceremonial or task layer, while repairable cotton continues in lower garments. A new wardrobe direction.

Feet and ground

Grippy water shoes for daily wet-ground use; barefoot in the depicted swim-training context; field shoes matched to the actual substrate.

06 · Third Voice · route C

Sané-Kora Institute

Intentional sound

Where the identifier moves

Silence and freedom of colour remain the rules. The full drape becomes an available ceremonial shape.

Feet and ground

Quiet soft sandals for daily use; barefoot on the depicted clean movement floor; field soles tested against the actual surface.

07 · Commons · route C

The Sund Commons

Shared maintenance

Where the identifier moves

The transferable garment system survives without a jacket: standard fasteners, spare allowances, replaceable panels and previous-wearer tabs move to shorts and apron.

Feet and ground

Repairable walking shoes; flexible training version; workshop footwear selected for the work.

05 · First headwear hypotheses

Weather. Ceremony.
An entrusted role.

Headwear can do more than complete an outfit. It can organise attention, carry a tool, reveal a lineage or mark a role that ends when the duty ends.

Each school chooses which of the three categories below it uses. “Temporary office” is a new worldbuilding possibility. Sund’s near-identical practical and ceremonial cap is deliberate.

01 · headwear

TKI

The wearer adjusts a frame, as a position taken.

Do not make the survey cap resemble a large generic graduation board. Test whether the visor obscures another person during conversation.

02 · headwear

Merikani

Value is held inside; the exterior stays calm.

The everyday illustration exposes more patterned waist cloth than the inward-value brief calls for. Reduce that exposure in the next detailed sheet.

03 · headwear

Temenggong

The tying method and the relationship to place matter more than a crown.

Keep the fold from becoming a generic royal turban. The earlier tension between visible rank and carried responsibility remains a design question.

04 · headwear

Lan Fang

The headpiece carries a revision history.

The generated everyday vest became more substantial than the proposed single-shoulder version. Explore a one-panel alternative before treating this cut as settled.

05 · headwear

Nine Rain

The hat is part of an account of water, use and repair; its numerical and ecological meanings belong to the Straits.

The weave marks carry invented meanings of their own. The canopy is ready for material tests as rain protection.

06 · headwear

Kora

Keep the listening anatomy open. The material is judged in motion as well as in portrait.

The ears-clear idea is functional and sits alongside personal and religious head coverings. Material and acoustic testing resolve the alternatives.

07 · headwear

Sund

Ceremonial care can change the meaning of an ordinary object without changing its silhouette.

Do not make the ceremonial version grand simply to match the others. A waist apron also needs its own hygiene and laundering allocation.

Hair remains its own design layer. Short cuts, tied hair, braids, locs, natural volume and wearer-specific coverings can work with these forms. A prototype accommodates those differences, and the hat fits the hair.

The uncovered head is also a valid option. Weather headwear is used when needed; a ceremonial rule needs a named occasion and wearing sequence. We can explore who removes, folds, exchanges or returns a headpiece before deciding it must always be worn.

to a lived garment.

HeadwearFold sequence, band adjustment, ear clearance, hair volume and wearing/removal gestures.Who can wear it comfortably, and what makes it specific to the school?

Character plateOne adult wearer in four occasions, with the same face, physique and clothing logic.Whether this is a real wardrobe family, beyond four pictures.

My strongest next trio: Temenggong’s fold and low leaf headpiece; Kora’s exposed shoulder and ears-clear soft structure; Nine Rain’s record band and repairable canopy. Merikani deserves a particularly careful close-up to keep its precious cloth genuinely inward.

07 · Development record

A new pass,
with its decisions visible.

Lin Wei’s revised coverage direction is recorded above. Formal figures are inherited from Part II; the open everyday, movement and light field diagrams are new. All headwear geometries and role systems in this volume are new.

Historical and regional costume analogues remain in Dress Atlas I. The earlier A/B wardrobe workshop remains available in Dress Atlas II. This volume makes no new claim of historical descent or authenticity.

Original SVG construction diagrams are paired with images made using the built-in image-generation tool. The image prompts and original generated PNGs are included in the downloadable package. The HTML embeds all its visuals for offline reading. No live website has been changed.
